title: A Few Good Men by Aaron Sorkin on Broadway #afewgoodmen #tomblyth #af...
transcript: A good courtroom drama is well paced, allegorical, and urgent. In its first Broadway revival, A Few Good Men accomplishes two of these. It follows three military lawyers defending a pair of marines who have been accused of murder, and discovering all the shady business behind it. Act 1 is a snooze fest of tedious but necessary exposition, while Act 2 focuses on the trial and is much more interesting. Still, the whole thing feels very procedural and while tightly paced and structured, the balance between character depth and plot development leans too heavily toward the latter for my taste. I don't think these elements should be mutually exclusive, and there are plenty of other plays that deliver on both fronts. This one keeps its cast on a tight leash, though Krysta Rodriguez and Tom Blyth do a solid job depicting the contrasting outlooks people have on their work and its impact. Daniel Kaffee is a military lawyer as a means to a personal end, while the more earnest Joanne Galloway believes in the work wholeheartedly. Neither character is developed much beyond their relationship to their work, but maybe that says something about the all-consuming nature of their jobs. The case that they're arguing does have thematic weight and provides a window into a culture that allows superiors to operate unquestioned, rules to be bent behind closed doors, and intimidation tactics to keep people in their place. I'm not sure, however, if we needed this revival to illuminate that these types of spaces exist — it's already abundantly clear to anyone who reads the news. This production feels timely but it doesn't contribute anything novel to the conversation, especially when the story has already been immortalized as an award-winning film. All that said, if you're looking for something to bring your dad to, this might be the one.
reasoning: Creator finds Act 1 tedious and the production thematically redundant, but acknowledges solid performances, tight pacing in Act 2, and suggests it as a dad-friendly outing. Overall lukewarm with notable reservations.
